page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at 3.5 GHz, supported by 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and encryption, as well as Geekbench ray tracing and image processing. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks are consistently in the top 25%. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

This server is configured for workloads requiring high resource density and local storage capacity, such as database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, which all register strong benchmark results. It supports basic machine learning tasks, achieving strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM models. However, text generation for larger models is a notable tradeoff, with the 70B model text generation falling into the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.
